biography.plain_text: Sean van Waes is a Belgian entrepreneur who developed Lazer Sport through a management buyout with colleague Peter Steenwegen. He held the majority stake when Shimano acquired the bicycle-helmet business in 2016. Based in Antwerp, he subsequently became a founding partner of Creative Capital Antwerp, investing in companies requiring financial and operational support.

long_biography.plain_text:
An uncomfortable helmet at his first Ironman in Lanzarote prompted Sean van Waes to enter the helmet business. The Lazer Sport entrepreneur wanted equipment that cyclists would choose to wear. He also devised a removable helmet cover, with fittings around its rim allowing riders to attach and remove it from either direction.

Product development at Lazer combined physical tests with computer simulations. During his leadership, the team developed KinetiCore, building impact-absorbing foam blocks into the helmet itself. Simulations allowed unsuitable designs to be rejected before expensive moulds were made. Researchers drew on vehicle crumple zones and tested thousands of helmets while refining the blocks.
